latest.title: Contract Wins and Uplifts Totalling £24m
latest.content:

RNS Number : 1322S
TPXimpact Holdings PLC
26 August 2026
26 August 2026
TPXimpact Holdings PLC
("TPXimpact", "TPX" or the "Group" or the "Company")
Contract Wins and Uplifts Totalling £24m
£19m contract uplift and one year extension secured with HM Land Registry and new £5m British Library award
TPXimpact Holdings PLC (AIM: TPX), a leading technology-enabled services company focused on people-powered digital transformation, is pleased to announce two significant contract developments with a combined value of
£24 million
.
HM Land Registry: £19m Contract Uplift
TPXimpact has secured a
£19 million contract uplift
and one year extension under its ongoing strategic delivery partnership with His Majesty's Land Registry (HMLR), extending the contract to May 2028. This extension builds on TPXimpact's appointment in May 2023 as HMLR's primary Digital, Data, and Technology (DDaT) Delivery Partner, originally awarded as a four-year contract to May 2027. The contract was awarded via an open and transparent process using the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework. This extension was included as part of the original contract.
The expanded funding reflects the ongoing growth and success of the joint delivery model, as TPXimpact and HMLR work together to modernise casework systems and accelerate HMLR's transition to a digital-first organisation.
British Library: £5m Contract Win
The Group's digital experience agency,
manifesto
, has recorded its largest ever win, having been selected as the successful bidder to provide digital product development services for the
British Library
as part of its landmark Future Web Programme.
●
Initial Contract Value:
£5 million
●
Contract Duration:
Initial 30-month term, with options to extend
●
Services:
Digital product development, maintenance, and ongoing enhancement of the British Library's web estate via an agile delivery model.
manifesto will supply a multidisciplinary delivery team working alongside British Library staff to modernise the British Library's digital services, expand online access to its collections, and provide a flexible delivery capability tailored to evolving programme needs.
Bjӧrn Conway, Chief Executive Officer of TPXimpact, commented:
"I am delighted with the continued progress being shown by the Group. Securing a further £19m uplift and one year extension with HM Land Registry alongside a major new £5m win with the British Library highlights the exceptional trust our public sector partners place in our delivery teams.
Since we were first appointed as HMLR's core DDaT Delivery Partner in May 2023 under a £49m contract, our joint teams have delivered tangible, modernising changes that directly improve service speed and data quality. Securing this uplift is a testament to the strength of this collaboration and our shared execution track record.
We are equally proud that our digital experience agency manifesto, has been selected by the British Library for its Future Web Programme. Helping one of the world's iconic cultural institutions broaden public access to its vast archives requires adaptable, human-centred digital design-a space where Manifesto excels.
These wins further strengthen our long-term order book and reinforce TPXimpact's position as a key digital transformation partner for the UK public sector."

latest.content:

TPXimpact Holdings PLC

13 August 2026
TPXimpact Holdings PLC
("TPXimpact", "TPX" or the "Group" or the "Company")
TPXimpact confirms £25 million contract with the Ministry of Justice
Further to its announcement dated 10 August and following the contract having been signed, TPXimpact Holdings PLC (AIM: TPX), a leading digital transformation partner, is pleased to confirm that it has been selected as the successful bidder for a
£25 million
, 3-year contract with the
Ministry of Justice (MoJ)
to provide Probation Digital Delivery for
Manage People on Probation (MPOP)
and
Probation User Services
.
Contract Highlights & Key Details
●
Contract Value:
£25 million
●
Contract Duration:
Initial 3-year term from 3 August 2026 to 2 August 2029, with an option to extend for a further 12 months to August 2030 (totalling up to 4 years).
●
Framework Procurement:
Awarded following a competitive selection process under Lot 2 (Digital Capability and Delivery Partner) of the
Digital Outcomes and Specialists 7 (DOS 7)
framework.
Björn Conway, Chief Executive Officer of TPXimpact, commented:
"We look forward to expanding our ongoing relationship with the Ministry of Justice on this critical digital transformation programme. Modernising probation services is essential to creating safer communities, empowering frontline staff, and delivering better outcomes for individuals within the justice system.
At a time when the public sector is under increasing pressure to deliver more with finite resources, digital transformation is one of the most effective levers available to improve productivity and service delivery. By equipping frontline teams with better tools, data and processes, organisations can increase capacity, reduce inefficiencies and achieve better outcomes for the people they serve.
This award underscores our position as a trusted digital partner to UK Central Government. I'm delighted with the start we have made to this year; securing this contract brings our total new business won in the first four months of FY27 to £58 million, reflecting excellent execution against our growth strategy and demonstrating strong ongoing demand for our capabilities."

company_30s.what_they_do: TPX Group is a technology specialist that builds and sells a cloud‑based platform for managing digital content and media workflows. The core product helps publishers, broadcasters and agencies organise, edit and deliver video, audio and text assets across multiple channels.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The digital‑content market is expanding faster than traditional media, driven by the shift to OTT, social‑video and the need for automated workflows. TPX’s platform sits at the intersection of content creation and distribution, giving it a defensible niche against larger cloud providers because it’s tightly integrated with media‑specific standards and offers a lower total cost of ownership for mid‑market operators.
company_30s.current_state: TPX is past the heavy‑burn phase and is now generating revenue through government and corporate contracts. It is in a growth mode, hiring to support new deals and has recently announced a £25 m contract with the Ministry of Justice. The share price is trading around 10 p, a fraction of its 12‑month high, reflecting the market’s current under‑appreciation of its contract pipeline.

rns_narrative: TPX has secured a sizeable £25 m deal with the UK Ministry of Justice, signalling a new revenue stream and a high‑profile customer that could lead to further public‑sector work.
The company has released its latest financials and corporate governance updates, including a share incentive plan to retain key staff and a major holdings notice that confirms institutional interest.
These announcements together suggest TPX is stabilising its cash flow, strengthening its balance sheet and positioning itself for a gradual rebound after a sharp sell‑off.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Bullish optimism driven by contract win, but wary of a 'sell‑the‑news' reaction
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Investors are excited about the MoJ contract and the potential for further public‑sector deals. The narrative focuses on the company’s ability to deliver on large projects and the upside from a growing digital‑content market.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some traders warn that the announcement could be a one‑off event and that the company’s revenue base remains thin. They fear a ‘sell‑the‑news’ pullback if the MoJ contract does not deliver the expected cash flow.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community moved from muted discussion to a flurry of bullish chatter after the MoJ contract was disclosed, but a handful of bearish posts caution that the market may still be skeptical.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for TPX is dead, indicating minimal public awareness and a high potential for surprise moves when new information hits.

near_term_catalysts: The MoJ contract announcement on 13 Aug 2026 is the most immediate trigger; a positive delivery update or a sign‑off could spark a rally.
The AGM and annual report will reveal whether TPX’s earnings meet expectations; a better‑than‑expected profit margin could validate the growth story.
A spike in trading volume above the 30‑day average, especially if accompanied by a break of the 20‑day moving average, would signal institutional buying and confirm a bottom.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to confirm the thesis are: 1) MoJ contract signing confirmation and a revenue lift in the next quarterly report; 2) Volume exceeding 1.5x the 30‑day average; 3) Price breaking a 60‑p support level, indicating a breakout from the deep trough.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early phase of a recovery cycle – the price has fallen well below its peak and the APEX compression score suggests a tight range that could snap. The next few months will be critical; a single catalyst or a volume surge can trigger a swift mean‑reversion.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: TPX’s recent contract win represents a tangible revenue boost and a validation of its product in a high‑value market. The deep sell‑off has wiped out most weak hands, leaving the share in a cheap position. If the price recovers to the 60‑70 p level (roughly the midpoint of the 52‑week range), the upside is about 6‑7× the current price. Historical data for deep‑bottom signals (green and orange) show average returns of 39‑113 % with win rates around 40‑45 %, giving a strong asymmetry favouring a long position.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The primary risk is that the MoJ deal may not materialise as expected or that TPX’s operating margins remain thin. If the company fails to deliver on the contract, the price could stay near the 10‑p floor, exposing the trade to a 90 % downside from the 12‑month high. A prolonged lack of volume and institutional interest would also undermine the mean‑reversion thesis.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: down to 10 p (≈ 90 % from the high). Potential gain: up to 60‑70 p (≈ 6‑7×). The reward far outweighs the risk, especially given the low entry price and the high probability of a rebound after a deep crash.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter around 30 p if the price breaks above the 20‑day moving average and volume spikes 1.5× the 30‑day average. Allocate 5 % of your portfolio to this position, set a stop at 20 p, and trail the stop at 70 % of the profit once the price moves above 50 p.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until the MoJ contract is officially signed and a positive earnings update is released. Look for a volume surge and a break of the 60‑p support level before committing.
playbook.if_passing: There are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks. The only terminal risk is a failure to deliver on the MoJ contract or a sustained lack of institutional interest, which would keep the price trapped at the low end.

ai_insights.bottom_line: TPX sits on a deep sell‑off, just hit a major contract win, and offers a high‑reward, low‑risk contrarian play if the price recovers to the 60‑p midpoint.
